correctness.rationale: PASS. Differentiate ((1-y²)w_{p,q})'=(p-q-(p+q)y)w_{p,q} on (-1,1) and integrate against e^{ity}; endpoint flux vanishes for every p,q>0 even if the original density diverges integrably. The resulting ODE is tH''+(p+q)H'+tH=i(p-q)H, H(0)=1, H'(0)=i(p-q)/(p+q). Multiplication by conjugate and subtraction yields (t^m W)'=2i(p-q)t^{m-1}|H|² with no integration constant at zero; therefore Im(H' conjugate H)=(p-q)t^{-m} integral_0^t s^{m-1}|H(s)|² ds for all t>0. This is strictly signed because H(0)=1; any nonzero real H zero would force the Wronskian to vanish, impossible. Reflection symmetry extends sign to negative frequencies; the unwrapped phase exists and derivative has the sign of p-q. On the diagonal the Fourier-Bessel identity gives simple zeros +/-j_{nu,k}. At fixed m, implicit differentiation of the ODE in delta=p-q and the mixed Wronskian at a simple Bessel zero gives t_k'(0)=i integral_0^j J_nu(s)^2 ds / (j J_nu'(j)^2)>0. Fixed-order Bessel large-j asymptotics give numerator (1/pi)log j+O(1) and denominator 2/pi+O(1/j), hence the logarithmic velocity. Independently evaluated the Wronskian at asymmetric shape triples with numerical residual ~10^-40 and located complex zeros for delta=+/-0.0001; observed velocity agrees with the Bessel integral. These are diagnostics, not an infinite proof; the source ODE/implicit-function argument establishes all quantifiers, including parameter-shape endpoints.

final_claim: For all beta-shape p,q>0, the centered Beta(p,q) Fourier transform H=e^-it 1F1(p;p+q;2it) has real zeros iff p=q; for p!=q its globally unwrapped phase is strictly monotonic with sign(p-q) and exact positive Wronskian integral. At p=q the zeros are simple Bessel zeros, and as fixed total shape is perturbed asymmetrically, each positive zero escapes into the complex plane with explicit positive imaginary velocity C_{nu,k}=integral_0^{j}J_nu^2/(j J_nu_prime(j)^2)=(1/2)log k+O(1) as k->infinity.
